# Multi-Pump Switching Control System - **Difficulty:** Medium (medium) ## Requirements In an industrial water supply system, there are 5 pumps, each of which can be controlled independently. The system needs to support both manual and automatic operating modes. Based on the value of the mode variable, switch to the corresponding operating mode. In manual mode, control the start and stop of the selected pump based on the value of pumpGroup[1..5].selection. In automatic mode, compare the priority of each pump, and automatically select the 3 pumps with higher priority for water supply according to the method of three in use and two on standby. ## Interface Definition | Direction | Variable/Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Input | `mode` | `BOOL` | FALSE: Manual mode
TRUE: Automatic mode | | Input | `start` | `BOOL` | Start button, used to start the manually selected or automatically selected pump | | Input | `stop` | `BOOL` | Stop button, used to stop all pumps | | Input/Output | `pumpGroup` | `ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_Pump` | Five pump records passed by reference. Read priority and selection; write only RunComd. | **Data type `ST_Pump`** | Field | Data Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `priority` | `INT` | Priority; larger values have higher priority. Read-only to the function block. | | `selection` | `BOOL` | Manual-selection state. Read-only to the function block. | | `RunComd` | `BOOL` | Run command written by the function block; TRUE runs and FALSE stops. |

(*--------------------------------------------------------------
  Data‑type for a single pump
--------------------------------------------------------------*)
TYPE ST_Pump : STRUCT
    priority  : INT;     // Read‑only priority (larger → higher priority)
    selection : BOOL;    // Read‑only manual‑selection flag
    RunComd   : BOOL;    // Write‑only run command (TRUE = start, FALSE = stop)
END_STRUCT
END_TYPE

(*--------------------------------------------------------------
  Multi‑pump switching control function block

  Inputs:
    mode   – FALSE = manual mode, TRUE = automatic mode
    start  – start push‑button (rising‑edge triggered)
    stop   – stop push‑button (rising‑edge triggered)

  In‑Out:
    pumpGroup – array of 5 pump records (priority & selection are read,
                RunComd is written)
--------------------------------------------------------------*)
FUNCTION_BLOCK MultiPumpControl
VAR_INPUT
    mode  : BOOL;   // FALSE = Manual, TRUE = Automatic
    start : BOOL;   // Start push‑button (rising edge)
    stop  : BOOL;   // Stop push‑button (rising edge)
END_VAR
VAR_IN_OUT
    pumpGroup : ARRAY[1..5] OF ST_Pump;
END_VAR
VAR
    startPrev : BOOL := FALSE;   // Edge‑detection memory for START
    stopPrev  : BOOL := FALSE;   // Edge‑detection memory for STOP
    i, j, tmp : INT;             // Loop counters & temp for sorting
    sortedIdx : ARRAY[1..5] OF INT; // Indices of pumps sorted by priority
END_VAR

(* -------------------------------------------------------------
   STOP – rising edge of the STOP button stops all pumps
   ------------------------------------------------------------- *)
IF stop AND NOT stopPrev THEN
    FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
        pumpGroup[i].RunComd := FALSE;
    END_FOR;
END_IF;
stopPrev := stop;

(* -------------------------------------------------------------
   START – rising edge of the START button starts the selected
   pump(s) in manual mode, or the three highest‑priority pumps
   in automatic mode.
   ------------------------------------------------------------- *)
IF start AND NOT startPrev THEN
    IF NOT mode THEN
        (* ---- Manual mode ---- *)
        (* Start every pump whose selection flag is TRUE *)
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            IF pumpGroup[i].selection THEN
                pumpGroup[i].RunComd := TRUE;
            END_IF;
        END_FOR;
    ELSE
        (* ---- Automatic mode ---- *)
        (* 1) Build a list of pump indices sorted by priority (descending) *)
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            sortedIdx[i] := i;
        END_FOR;

        (* Simple bubble‑sort (stable) – fine for only 5 pumps *)
        FOR i := 1 TO 4 DO
            FOR j := i+1 TO 5 DO
                IF pumpGroup[sortedIdx[j]].priority > pumpGroup[sortedIdx[i]].priority THEN
                    tmp := sortedIdx[i];
                    sortedIdx[i] := sortedIdx[j];
                    sortedIdx[j] := tmp;
                END_IF;
            END_FOR;
        END_FOR;

        (* 2) Drive the three highest‑priority pumps, keep the rest on standby *)
        FOR i := 1 TO 5 DO
            IF i <= 3 THEN
                pumpGroup[sortedIdx[i]].RunComd := TRUE;   // start
            ELSE
                pumpGroup[sortedIdx[i]].RunComd := FALSE;  // standby
            END_IF;
        END_FOR;
    END_IF;
END_IF;
startPrev := start;

END_FUNCTION_BLOCK
